title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mountain Brook, AL

metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mountain Brook, AL | Old AL Estates
metaDescription: Inherited mineral rights tied to Mountain Brook, AL family land elsewhere in Alabama? We research the title and make a straightforward offer, no pressure.
heroLead: Mountain Brook itself was never mined or drilled, but plenty of the families who live here today hold mineral interests their grandparents kept from farmland, timber tracts, or coal leases elsewhere in Alabama.
intro: We get a specific kind of call from Mountain Brook: a mineral interest that has nothing to do with the address itself. It's usually a fraction of a coalbed methane unit up in north Jefferson or Walker County, or a royalty tied to south Alabama acreage a great-grandparent farmed before the family moved into Birmingham's suburbs generations ago. The interest gets mentioned in an estate, nobody's entirely sure what it's worth or even exactly where it sits, and it sits untouched for another decade until someone decides to finally sort it out.

sections.heading: When the Interest and the Address Don't Match
paragraphs: If what you're holding is a legal description on an old deed rather than a producing well you can point to, the first step is simply locating it — confirming the county, the section, and whether the interest is still intact after passing through one or more estates. We do that research ourselves, wherever in Alabama the actual acreage sits.

sections.heading: Estate Interests Nobody Has Looked At in Years
paragraphs: Mineral interests that come through a probate file often sit dormant because no one wants to spend the time chasing down what a fractional interest in a decades-old lease is actually worth. That's the exact situation we're set up to handle — send us the deed, the legal description, or even just the county it's supposed to be in, and we'll tell you plainly what we find before you decide anything.

faqs.question: We know we have a mineral interest somewhere in Alabama but not exactly where. Can you help find it?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Give us whatever documentation you have — an old deed, a probate file, even just a family memory of the county — and we'll research the courthouse record to locate it.

faqs.question: It's a small fraction from an estate years ago. Is it worth the trouble to sell?
faqs.answer: Small fractions do have value, particularly if the underlying unit is producing. We'll give you an honest number once we've confirmed what's actually there.

faqs.question: Do we need a probate attorney before talking to you?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily to start the conversation. If title needs to be cleared through probate, we'll tell you exactly what's needed once we've reviewed the record.
